resolutions.researcher_notes: Unit was DEAD_LINK: the only citation (iraqieconomists.net Al-Jibawi PDF) is live (HTTP 200) but on WebFetch its text does NOT mention Akkas/Okaz, Anbar pipelines, or a T1-K3 segment at all — it is a misattributed citation, so it cannot support the Status. Kept as ok=false/contains_value=false. GEM entity = a PROPOSED 3-segment gas trunk from the Okaz (Akkas) field via stations T1 and K3 to Al-Anbar (T1-K3 = 26in, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil); this is the wider gas-TRANSPORT network, distinct from the short ~30km line that already feeds the adjacent Akkas power station. Corroborated 'proposed' with two independent professional outlets: (1) The National (2025-07-22) — 'Additional contracts will be signed to build surface installations and lay pipelines connecting the wells to central processing units,' gas then directed to the Anbar Combined Cycle Power Plant (still under construction) = pipeline network planned, not built, owner Iraqi Ministry of Oil. (2) MEES (2025-07-25) — states current output (~40mn cfd) runs via an existing 30km line to the Akkas power plant, while SCOP will ADD new flow lines from SLB-drilled wells to new processing units under a forthcoming contract = the expanded transport pipelines are planned. Both distinguish the built local feed from the still-to-be-built transport network, matching Status=proposed. Tier high: two reputable independent outlets each with their own operational reporting; caveat — both cover the same July 2025 SLB/Akkas award, though the qualitative 'planned pipeline network' status is also consistent with earlier (2022) MEES and Iraq Oil Report coverage. iraq-businessnews.com/2025/07/22 aggregator returned HTTP 401 (not usable).
